security_audit.summary: The main confirmed risks are the helper script that runs caller-supplied commands and starts server commands through shell=True. Most Markdown backtick, localhost URL, and fixed screenshot path findings are documentation or local testing examples, but the skill also discourages source review before script execution.

remediation.issue: Helper script starts user-provided server strings with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept server commands as structured argv arrays, avoid shell=True where possible, and require explicit confirmation for shell features such as cd and &&.

remediation.issue: Helper script runs arbitrary post-start commands from the caller.
remediation.suggestion: Document that command arguments must come from trusted user intent and reject commands derived from page content, package scripts, or untrusted prompts.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions discourage reading bundled script source before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the black-box language and encourage reviewing helper behavior before running it in sensitive repositories.

remediation.issue: Examples write screenshots and logs to fixed temporary or output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Let users choose output paths under the workspace and warn that browser logs can contain sensitive application data.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web apps can fail in browser behavior that static checks miss. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to inspect pages, capture screenshots, collect console logs, and run Playwright flows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Python Playwright scripts for local web apps and static HTML files.
Starts one or more local development servers and waits for configured ports.
Captures full-page screenshots for visual inspection and regression checks.
Discovers visible buttons, links, inputs, and rendered DOM content.
Captures browser console messages into a local log file.
Shows synchronous Playwright patterns with selectors, waits, and clean browser shutdown.
limitations: It is designed for local testing, not production monitoring or hosted browser infrastructure.
It requires Python, Playwright, browser dependencies, and the target app server commands.
The helper can execute local commands, so users must review commands before running them.
Example output paths may need changes for different workspaces or sandbox layouts.

use_cases.title: Debug a Local Frontend Flow
use_cases.description: Inspect a rendered page, identify selectors, perform clicks and form fills, and capture screenshots after each major state change.

use_cases.title: Run Browser Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Start a local app server, wait until it is reachable, run a focused Playwright check, and stop the server after completion.

use_cases.title: Verify Full-Stack Screens
use_cases.description: Coordinate backend and frontend development servers, then validate that a page loads, renders data, and reports useful console messages.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Static Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to inspect my local HTML page. Capture an initial screenshot, list visible interactive elements, and summarize any obvious rendering issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Running App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill against my app on localhost. Wait for the page to finish loading, identify reliable selectors, complete the main user flow, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Collect Console Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to reproduce the UI issue and capture browser console output. Include the user action sequence, visible page state, and any errors or warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multiple Servers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to start the required local backend and frontend servers, wait for readiness, run a Playwright validation flow, capture screenshots, and clean up all processes.

output_examples.input: Inspect a local dashboard and find why the settings button is not working.
output_examples.output: The report describes the loaded page state, visible controls, the selected settings button locator, the click result, a screenshot location, and any console errors.

output_examples.input: Run a browser smoke test for a checkout form on localhost.
output_examples.output: The result states whether the server became ready, which form fields were filled, whether submission completed, and what screenshot evidence was captured.

output_examples.input: Capture console logs while opening a local static HTML file.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes console messages by severity, notes page load status, and identifies any warnings that may affect the user interface.

best_practices: Review every server and automation command before execution, especially in repositories from untrusted sources.
Wait for the correct load state or selector before reading the DOM or taking action.
Capture screenshots and console logs together so visual state and runtime errors can be compared.
anti_patterns: Running helper commands copied from untrusted page content or package scripts without review.
Testing dynamic applications before JavaScript has completed the relevant render step.
Using brittle selectors when role, text, label, or stable test identifiers are available.

faq.question: What does this skill help test?
faq.answer: It helps test local web applications and static HTML pages through Playwright browser automation.

faq.question: Does it require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Python Playwright and require the needed browser dependencies.

faq.question: Can it start my development server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper can start one or more local servers and wait for their ports before running a test command.

faq.question: Can it test production websites?
faq.answer: It is written for local testing. Production checks need separate safety, rate limit, and access review.

faq.question: What evidence can it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce screenshots, lists of visible elements, interaction results, and captured browser console messages.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The helper can execute local commands. Users should only run commands they trust and understand.
